children.text: prathamo 'ṅkaḥ --
children.translated_text: Act One —

children.text: yā sṛṣṭiḥ sraṣṭur ādyā vahati vidhihutaṃ yā havir yā ca hotrī
ye dve kālaṃ vidhattaḥ śrutiviṣayaguṇā yā sthitā vyāpya viśvam /
children.translated_text: the two [sun and moon] who ordain time, she [the ether] who pervades the universe, abiding as the object of hearing;
She who is the Creator's first creation, she who bears the oblation offered by sacred rite, and she who is the sacrificing priestess;

children.text: yām āhuḥ sarvabījaprakṛtir iti yayā prāṇinaḥ prāṇavantaḥ
pratyakṣābhiḥ prapannas tanubhir avatu vas tābhir aṣṭābhir īśaḥ //
children.translated_text: may the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) protect you through those eight manifest forms of his!
she whom they call the <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the origin of all seeds, and she by whom living beings possess life —

children.text: yā sṛṣṭiḥ sraṣṭur ādyā vahati vidhi-hutaṃ yā havir yā ca hotrī
ye dve kālaṃ vidhattaḥ śruti-viṣaya-guṇā yā sthitā vyāpya viśvam /
yām āhuḥ sarva-bīja-prakṛtir iti yayā prāṇinaḥ prāṇavantaḥ
pratyakṣābhiḥ prapannas tanubhir avatu vas tābhir aṣṭābhir īśaḥ //
sūtradhāraḥ  ārya abhirūpabhūyiṣṭhā pariṣad iyam / adya khalu kālidāsagrathitavastunā
children.translated_text: <s>Sūtradhāra</s> (Stage-Director): Noble lady, this audience is mostly composed of discerning people. Today indeed, we must present before them

children.text: sūtra-dhāraḥ -- ārya abhirūpa-bhūyiṣṭhā pariṣad iyam / adya khalu kāli-dāsa-grathita-vastunā
navenābhijñānaśākuntalākhyena nāṭakenopasthātavyam asmābhiḥ / tat pratipātram ādhīyatāṃ yatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: a new drama called the <s>Abhijñānaśākuntala</s>, composed by <s>Kālidāsa</s>. Therefore, let effort be applied to each role.

children.text: navena abhijñāna-śākuntala-ākhyena nāṭakena upasthātavyam asmābhiḥ / tat pratipātram ādhīyatāṃ yatnaḥ /
naṭī  suvihitaprayogatayāryasya na kim api parihāsyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Naṭī</s> (Actress): With the master's performance so well-arranged, nothing at all will be found wanting.

children.text: naṭī -- suvihita-prayogatayā āryasya na kim api parihāsyate /
sūtradhāraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sūtradhāra</s>:

children.text: sūtra-dhāraḥ --
ārye kathayāmi te bhūtārtham /
children.translated_text: Noble lady, I tell you the truth —

children.text: ārye kathayāmi te bhūta-artham /
ā paritoṣād viduṣāṃ na sādhu manye prayogavijñānam /
children.translated_text: Until the learned are satisfied, I do not consider my knowledge of dramatic art to be good;

children.text: balavad api śikṣitānām ātmany apratyayaṃ cetaḥ //
children.translated_text: for even the well-trained have minds that lack confidence in themselves.

children.text: ā paritoṣād viduṣāṃ na sādhu manye prayoga-vijñānam /
balavad api śikṣitānām ātmany apratyayaṃ cetaḥ //
naṭī  ārya evam etat / anantarakaraṇīyam ārya ājñāpayatu /
children.translated_text: <s>Naṭī</s>: Noble sir, so it is. Let the master command what is to be done next.

children.text: naṭī --- ārya evam etat / anantara-karaṇīyam ārya ājñāpayatu /
sūtradhāraḥ  kim anyad asyāḥ pariṣadaḥ śrutiprasādanataḥ / tad imam eva tāvad acirapravṛttam upabhogakṣamaṃ grīṣmasamayam adhikṛtya gīyatām / saṃprati hi
children.translated_text: <s>Sūtradhāra</s>: What else but pleasing the ears of this audience? Then, taking as our theme this recently arrived summer season, fit for enjoyment, let a song be sung. For now indeed —

children.text: sūtra-dhāraḥ -- kim anyad asyāḥ pariṣadaḥ śruti-prasādanataḥ / tad imam eva tāvad acira-pravṛttam upabhoga-kṣamaṃ grīṣma-samayam adhikṛtya gīyatām / saṃprati hi
subhagasalilāvagāhāḥ pāṭalasaṃsargasurabhivanavātāḥ /
children.translated_text: with pleasant immersions in cool water, with forest breezes fragrant from contact with <s>pāṭala</s> (trumpet-flower) blossoms,

children.text: pracchāyasulabhanidrā divasāḥ pariṇāmaramaṇīyāḥ //
children.translated_text: with easy sleep in the shade — the days are delightful in their ripening [heat].

children.text: subhaga-salila-avagāhāḥ pāṭala-saṃsarga-surabhi-vana-vātāḥ /
pracchāya-sulabha-nidrā divasāḥ pariṇāma-ramaṇīyāḥ //
naṭī  tathā (iti gāyati)
children.translated_text: <s>Naṭī</s>: So be it. (She sings:)

children.text: naṭī -- tathā (iti gāyati)
īṣadīṣaccumbitāni bhramaraiḥ sukumārakesaraśikhāni /
children.translated_text: Lightly, lightly kissed by bees on their delicate filament-tips,

children.text: avataṃsayanti damamānāḥ pramadāḥ śirīṣakusumāni //
children.translated_text: the playful young women tuck <s>śirīṣa</s> (silk-cotton) blossoms behind their ears.

children.text: īṣad-īṣac-cumbitāni bhramaraiḥ sukumāra-kesara-śikhāni /
avataṃsayanti damamānāḥ pramadāḥ śirīṣa-kusumāni //
sūtradhāraḥ  ārya sādhu gītam / aho rāgabaddhacittavṛttir ālikhita iva sarvato raṅgaḥ / tad idānīṃ katamatprakaraṇam āśritya enam ārādhayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūtradhāra</s>: Noble lady, well sung! Ah, with the minds of the audience bound by the melody, the entire theater seems as if painted still. Now, taking up which subject shall we gratify them?

children.text: sūtra-dhāraḥ -- ārya sādhu gītam / aho rāga-baddha-citta-vṛttir ālikhita iva sarvato raṅgaḥ / tad idānīṃ katamat-prakaraṇam āśritya enam ārādhayāmaḥ /
naṭī  nanv āryamiśraiḥ prathamam evājñaptam abhijñānaśakuntalaṃ nāma apūrvaṃ nāṭakaṃ prayoge adhikriyatām iti /
children.translated_text: <s>Naṭī</s>: Why, it was the honored master himself who first commanded: 'Let the unprecedented drama called the <s>Abhijñānaśākuntala</s> be undertaken for performance!'

children.text: naṭī -- nanv ārya-miśraiḥ prathamam evā ajñaptam abhijñāna-śakuntalaṃ nāma apūrvaṃ nāṭakaṃ prayoge adhikriyatām iti /
sūtradhāraḥ  ārye samyaganubhodhito 'smi / asmin kṣaṇe vismṛtaṃ khalu mayā tat / kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūtradhāra</s>: Noble lady, I have been rightly reminded! At this very moment I had indeed forgotten it. How so?

children.text: sūtra-dhāraḥ -- ārye samyag-anubhodhito 'smi / asmin kṣaṇe vismṛtaṃ khalu mayā tat / kutaḥ /
tavāsmi gītarāgeṇa hāriṇā prasabhaṃ hṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: I have been forcibly carried away by the captivating melody of your song;

children.text: eṣa rājeva duṣyantaḥ sāraṅgeṇātiraṃsahā //
children.translated_text: just as this King <s>Duṣyanta</s> [is carried away] by the antelope — he who cannot resist the chase.

children.text: tava asmi gīta-rāgeṇa hāriṇā prasabhaṃ hṛtaḥ /
eṣa rāja īva duṣyantaḥ sāraṅgeṇa atiraṃsahā //
(iti niṣkrāntau )
children.translated_text: (Thus they both exit.)

children.text: (iti niṣkrāntau )
(prasthāvanā)
children.translated_text: (End of Prologue.)

children.text: (prasthāvanā)
(tataḥ praviśati mṛgānusārī saśaracāpahasto rājā rathena sūtaś ca)
children.translated_text: (Then enters the King, pursuing a deer, bow and arrow in hand, on a chariot, together with the Charioteer.)

children.text: (tataḥ praviśati mṛga-anusārī saśara-cāpa-hasto rājā rathena sūtaś ca)
sūtaḥ  (rājānaṃ mṛtaṃ cāvalokya) āyuṣman /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (Charioteer): (Looking at the King and the deer) Long-lived one!

children.text: sūtaḥ -- (rājānaṃ mṛtaṃ ca avalokya) āyuṣman /
kṛṣṇasāre dadac cakṣus tvayi cādhijyakārmuke /
children.translated_text: Fixing your gaze upon the black antelope, and [seeing] you with bow strung,

children.text: mṛgānusāriṇaṃ sākṣāt paśyāmīva+pinākinam //
children.translated_text: I seem to behold the very <s>Pinākin</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) himself pursuing the deer.

children.text: kṛṣṇa-sāre dadac cakṣus tvayi ca adhijya-kārmuke /
mṛga-anusāriṇaṃ sākṣāt paśyāmi iva+pinākinam //
rājā  sūta dūram amunā sāraṅgeṇa vayam ākṛṣṭāḥ / ayaṃ punar itānīm api
children.translated_text: King: Charioteer, we have been drawn far by this antelope. And even now

children.text: rājā -- sūta dūram amunā sāraṅgeṇa vayam ākṛṣṭāḥ / ayaṃ punar itānīm api
grīvābhaṅgābhirāmaṃ muhur anupatati syandane dattadṛṣṭiḥ
paścārdhena praviṣṭaḥ śarapatanabhayād bhūyasā pūrvakāyam /
children.translated_text: his hindquarters drawn in from fear of the falling arrow, his forebody stretched far out,
repeatedly glancing back at the chariot, with his neck-bend charmingly [turned],

children.text: darbhair ardhāvalīḍhaiḥ śramavivṛtamukhabhraṃśibhiḥ kīrṇavartmā
paśyodagraplutatvād viyati bahutaraṃ stokam urvyāṃ prayāti //
children.translated_text: see! leaping high, he traverses more of the sky than of the earth.
his path strewn with half-chewed <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) dropping from his fatigue-gaping mouth —

children.text: grīva-ābhaṅga-abhirāmaṃ muhur anupatati syandane datta-dṛṣṭiḥ
paśca-ardhena praviṣṭaḥ śara-patana-bhayād bhūyasā pūrva-kāyam /
darbhair ardha-avalīḍhaiḥ śrama-vivṛta-mukha-bhraṃśibhiḥ kīrṇa-vartmā
paśya udagra-plutatvād viyati bahutaraṃ stokam urvyāṃ prayāti //
(savismayam) tad eṣa katham anupatata eva me prayatnaprekṣaṇīyaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: (With wonder) How is it that even as I pursue him, he has become difficult to see even with effort?

children.text: (savismayam) tad eṣa katham anupatata eva me prayatna-prekṣaṇīyaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ /
sūtaḥ  āyuṣmann udghātinī bhūmir iti mayā raśmisaṃyamanād rathasya mandīkṛto vegaḥ / tena mṛga eṣa viprakṛṣṭāntaraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / saṃprati samadeśavartinas te na durāsado bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: Long-lived one, since the ground was rising, I slowed the chariot's speed by reining in. Therefore this deer has gained a great distance. Now, on level ground, he will not be difficult to reach.

children.text: sūtaḥ -- āyuṣmann udghātinī bhūmir iti mayā raśmi-saṃyamanād rathasya mandī-kṛto vegaḥ / tena mṛga eṣa viprakṛṣṭa-antaraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / saṃprati sama-deśa-vartinas te na durāsado bhaviṣyati /
rājā  tena hi mucyantām abhīṣavaḥ /
children.translated_text: King: Then loosen the reins!

children.text: rājā -- tena hi mucyantām abhīṣavaḥ /
sūtaḥ  yad ājñāpayaty āyuṣmān / (rathavegaṃ nirūpya) āyuṣman paśya paśya /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: As the long-lived one commands. (Indicating the chariot's speed) Long-lived one, look, look!

children.text: sūtaḥ -- yad ājñāpayaty āyuṣmān / (ratha-vegaṃ nirūpya) āyuṣman paśya paśya /
mukteṣu raśmiṣu nirāyatapūrvakāyā
niṣkampacāmaraśikhā nibhṛtordhvakarṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: their crest-plumes of <s>cāmara</s> (yak-tail) motionless, their ears held stiffly upright,
With the reins released, their forebodies stretched forward,

children.text: ātmoddhatair api rajobhir alaṅghanīyā
dhāvanty amī mṛgajavākṣamayeva+rathyāḥ //
children.translated_text: these chariot-horses run as if rendering the deer's speed insignificant.
outstripping even the dust raised by themselves,

children.text: mukteṣu raśmiṣu nirāyata-pūrva-kāyā
niṣkampa-cāmara-śikhā nibhṛta-ūrdhva-karṇāḥ /
ātma-uddhatair api rajobhir alaṅghanīyā
dhāvanty amī mṛga-java-akṣamaya īva+rathyāḥ //
rājā  satyam / atītya harito harīṃś ca vartante vājinaḥ / tathā hi /
children.translated_text: King: Truly! The horses surpass even <s>Hari's</s> (<s>Indra's</s>) steeds. For indeed —

children.text: rājā -- satyam / atītya harito harīṃś ca vartante vājinaḥ / tathā hi /
yad āloke sūkṣmaṃ vrajati sahasā tadvipulatām
yad ardhe vicchinnaṃ bhavati kṛtasaṃdhānam iva tat /
children.translated_text: what is split in half appears as if rejoined;
What appears minute at a distance suddenly attains vastness;

children.text: prakṛṣtyā yad vakraṃ tad api samarekhaṃ nayanayor
na me dūre kiṃcit kṣaṇam api na pārśve rathajavāt //
children.translated_text: nothing is far from me even for a moment, nor at my side, due to the chariot's speed.
what is by nature curved appears straight to the eyes —

children.text: yad āloke sūkṣmaṃ vrajati sahasā tad-vipulatām
yad ardhe vicchinnaṃ bhavati kṛta-saṃdhānam iva tat /
prakṛṣtyā yad vakraṃ tad api sama-rekhaṃ nayanayor
na me dūre kiṃcit kṣaṇam api na pārśve ratha-javāt //
sūta paśya enaṃ vyāpadyamānam / (iti śarasaṃdhānaṃ nāṭayati)
children.translated_text: Charioteer, watch him being overtaken! (He mimes fitting an arrow.)

children.text: sūta paśya enaṃ vyāpadyamānam / (iti śara-saṃdhānaṃ nāṭayati)
(nepathye)
children.translated_text: (From behind the scenes:)

children.text: (nepathye)
bho bho rājann āśramamṛgo 'yaṃ na hanvavyo na hantavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ho, ho, O King! This is a hermitage deer — it must not be killed, must not be killed!'

children.text: bho bho rājann āśrama-mṛgo 'yaṃ na hanvavyo na hantavyaḥ /
sūta  (ākarṇyāvalokya ca) āyuṣmann asya khalu te bāṇapātavartinaḥ kṛṣṭasārasyāntare tapasvina upasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: (Listening and looking) Long-lived one, ascetics have placed themselves between you and this black antelope that is within arrow-range.

children.text: sūta -- (ākarṇya avalokya ca) āyuṣmann asya khalu te bāṇa-pāta-vartinaḥ kṛṣṭa-sārasya antare tapasvina upasthitāḥ /
rājā  (sasaṃbhramam) tena hi pragṛhyantāṃ vājinaḥ /
children.translated_text: King: (Startled) Then hold back the horses!

children.text: rājā -- (sasaṃbhramam) tena hi pragṛhyantāṃ vājinaḥ /
sūta  tathā / (iti rathaṃ sthāpayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: So be it. (He halts the chariot.)

children.text: sūta -- tathā / (iti rathaṃ sthāpayati)
vaikhānasaḥ  (hastam udyamya) rājann āśramamṛgo 'yaṃ na hantavyo na hantavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikhānasa</s> (Hermit): (Raising his hand) O King, this is a hermitage deer — it must not be killed, must not be killed!

children.text: vaikhānasaḥ -- (hastam udyamya) rājann āśrama-mṛgo 'yaṃ na hantavyo na hantavyaḥ /
na khalu na khalu bāṇaḥ saṃnipātyo 'yam asmin mṛduni mṛgaśarīre puṣparāśāv+ivāgniḥ /
children.translated_text: Surely, surely this arrow must not be discharged upon this tender deer-body — like fire upon a heap of flowers!

children.text: kva bata hariṇakānāṃ jīvitaṃ cātilolaṃ kva ca niśitanipātā vajrasārāḥ śarās te //
children.translated_text: How [can you compare] the exceedingly fragile life of deer with your arrows, hard as diamond, falling with sharpened [points]?

children.text: na khalu na khalu bāṇaḥ saṃnipātyo 'yam asmin mṛduni mṛga-śarīre puṣpa-rāśāv+iva agniḥ /
kva bata hariṇakānāṃ jīvitaṃ ca atilolaṃ kva ca niśita-nipātā vajra-sārāḥ śarās te //
tat sādhukṛtasaṃdhānaṃ pratisaṃhara sāyakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, withdraw the well-fitted arrow;

children.text: ārtatrāṇāya vaḥ śastraṃ na prahartum anāgasi //
children.translated_text: your weapon is for the protection of the afflicted, not for striking the innocent.

children.text: tat sādhu-kṛta-saṃdhānaṃ pratisaṃhara sāyakam /
ārta-trāṇāya vaḥ śastraṃ na prahartum anāgasi //
rājā  eṣa pratisaṃhṛtaḥ (iti yathoktaṃ karoti)
children.translated_text: King: It is withdrawn. (He does as directed.)

children.text: rājā -- eṣa pratisaṃhṛtaḥ (iti yatha ūktaṃ karoti)
vaikhānasaḥ  sadṛśam etat puruvaṃśapradīpasya bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikhānasa</s>: This is worthy of you, the lamp of the <s>Puru</s> dynasty.

children.text: vaikhānasaḥ -- sadṛśam etat puru-vaṃśa-pradīpasya bhavataḥ /
janma yasya puror vaṃśe yuktarūpam idaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: Born as you are in the lineage of <s>Puru</s>, this [conduct] is fitting for you;

children.text: putram evaṃ guṇopetaṃ cakravartinam āpnuhi //
children.translated_text: may you obtain a son endowed with such virtues, a universal sovereign!

children.text: janma yasya puror vaṃśe yukta-rūpam idaṃ tava /
putram evaṃ guṇa-upetaṃ cakra-vartinam āpnuhi //
itarau  (bāhū udyamya) sarvathā cakravartinaṃ putram āpnuhi /
children.translated_text: The other two: (Raising their arms) By all means, may you obtain a son who will be a universal sovereign!

children.text: itarau -- (bāhū udyamya) sarvathā cakra-vartinaṃ putram āpnuhi /
(sapraṇāmam) pratigṛtītaṃ brāhmaṇavacanam /
children.translated_text: (With a bow) The words of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are accepted.

children.text: (sapraṇāmam) pratigṛtītaṃ brāhmaṇa-vacanam /
vaikhānsa  rājan samidāharaṇāya prasthitā vayam /eṣa khalu kaṇvasya kulapater anumālinītīram āśramo dṛśyate / na ced anyakāryātipātaḥ praviśya pratigṛhyatām ātitheyaḥ satkāraḥ / api ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikhānasa</s>: O King, we have set out to gather sacrificial wood. Here, on the bank of the <s>Mālinī</s> river, the hermitage of <s>Kaṇva</s>, the patriarch, is visible. If you have no other pressing engagement, please enter and accept the hospitality due to a guest. Moreover —

children.text: vaikhānsa -- rājan samid-āharaṇāya prasthitā vayam /eṣa khalu kaṇvasya kula-pater anumālinī-tīram āśramo dṛśyate / na ced anya-kārya-atipātaḥ praviśya pratigṛhyatām ātitheyaḥ satkāraḥ / api ca /
ramyās tapodhanānāṃ pratihatavighnāḥ kriyāḥ samavalokya /
children.translated_text: Observing the rites of the ascetics proceeding unobstructed and delightful,

children.text: jñāsyasi kiyadbhujo me rakṣati maurvīkiṇāṅka iti //
children.translated_text: you will know how much this arm of mine, scarred by the bowstring's mark, protects.

children.text: ramyās tapodhanānāṃ pratihata-vighnāḥ kriyāḥ samavalokya /
jñāsyasi kiyad-bhujo me rakṣati maurvī-kiṇa-aṅka iti //
rājā  api saṃnihito 'tra kulapatiḥ /
children.translated_text: King: Is the patriarch present here?

children.text: rājā -- api saṃnihito 'tra kula-patiḥ /
vaikhānasa  idānīm eva duhitaraṃ śakuntalām atithisatkārāya niyujya daivam asyāḥ pratikūlaṃ śamayituṃ somatīrthaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikhānasa</s>: Just now, having appointed his daughter <s>Śakuntalā</s> to attend to the hospitality of guests, he has gone to <s>Somatīrtha</s> to propitiate the adverse fate [threatening] her.

children.text: vaikhānasa -- idānīm eva duhitaraṃ śakuntalām atithi-satkārāya niyujya daivam asyāḥ pratikūlaṃ śamayituṃ soma-tīrthaṃ gataḥ /
rājā  bhavatu / tām eva paśyāmi / sā khalu viditabhaktiṃ māṃ maharṣeḥ kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: King: Very well. I shall see her. She will surely make my devotion known to the great sage.

children.text: rājā -- bhavatu / tām eva paśyāmi / sā khalu vidita-bhaktiṃ māṃ maharṣeḥ kariṣyati /
vaikhānasa  sādhayāmas tāvat (iti saśiṣyo niṣkrāntaḥ)
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikhānasa</s>: Let us proceed then. (He exits with his pupils.)

children.text: vaikhānasa -- sādhayāmas tāvat (iti saśiṣyo niṣkrāntaḥ)
rājā  sūta codayāśvān puṇyāśramadarśanena tāvad ātmānaṃ punīmahe /
children.translated_text: King: Charioteer, urge the horses forward! Let us purify ourselves by the sight of the holy hermitage.

children.text: rājā -- sūta codaya aśvān puṇya-āśrama-darśanena tāvad ātmānaṃ punīmahe /
sūta  yad ājñāpayaty āyuṣman / (iti bhūyo ratha evaṃ nirūpayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: As the long-lived one commands. (He again indicates the chariot's [movement].)

children.text: sūta -- yad ājñāpayaty āyuṣman / (iti bhūyo ratha evaṃ nirūpayati)
rājā  (samantād avalokya) sūta akathito 'pi jñāyata eva yathāyam āśramābhogas tapovanasyeti /
children.translated_text: King: (Looking all around) Charioteer, even without being told, one knows that this is the precincts of an ascetic grove. How so?

children.text: rājā -- (samantād avalokya) sūta akathito 'pi jñāyata eva yatha āyam āśramā abhogas tapo-vanasya iti /
sūta  katham iva /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: How indeed?

children.text: sūta -- katham iva /
rājā  kiṃ na paśyati bhavān / iha hi
children.translated_text: King: Do you not see? For here —

children.text: rājā -- kiṃ na paśyati bhavān / iha hi
nīvārāḥ śukagarbhakoṭaramukhabhraṣṭās tarūṇām adhaḥ
prasnigdhāḥ kvacid iṅgudīphālabhidaḥ sūcyanta evopalāḥ /
children.translated_text: stones are seen here and there, glistening where <s>iṅgudī</s> (nut) shells have been cracked;
Beneath the trees, grains of wild rice dropped from the hollows of parrot-nests;

children.text: viśvāsopagamād abhinnagatayaḥ śabdaṃ sahante mṛgās
toyādhārapathāś ca valkalaśikhāniṣyandarekhāṅkitāḥ //
children.translated_text: and the water-channel paths are marked with streaks of dripping from the edges of bark-garments.
deer, their gait unbroken through trust, endure [our] noise;

children.text: nīvārāḥ śuka-garbha-koṭara-mukha-bhraṣṭās tarūṇām adhaḥ
prasnigdhāḥ kvacid iṅgudī-phāla-bhidaḥ sūcyanta eva upalāḥ /
viśvāsa-upagamād abhinna-gatayaḥ śabdaṃ sahante mṛgās
toya-ādhāra-pathāś ca valkala-śikhā-niṣyanda-rekhā-aṅkitāḥ //
kulyāmbhobhiḥ pavanacapalaiḥ śākhino dhautamūlā
bhinno rāgaḥ kisalayarucām ājyadhūmodgamena /
children.translated_text: the color of their young shoots altered by the rising smoke of clarified butter —
The trees, their roots washed by the wavering waters of the irrigation channels,

children.text: ete cārvāgupavanabhuvi chinnadarbhāṅkurāyām
naṣṭāṃśakā hariṇaśiśavo mandamandaṃ caranti //
children.translated_text: fawn-calves, their [fear of] stumbling gone, move slowly, slowly.
and here, on the garden-ground with its cropped <s>darbha</s>-grass sprouts,

children.text: kulya-ambhobhiḥ pavana-capalaiḥ śākhino dhauta-mūlā
bhinno rāgaḥ kisalaya-rucām ājya-dhūma-udgamena /
ete ca arvāg-upavana-bhuvi chinna-darbha-aṅkurāyām
naṣṭa-aṃśakā hariṇa-śiśavo manda-mandaṃ caranti //
sūta  sarvam upapannam /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: Everything is fitting.

children.text: sūta -- sarvam upapannam /
rājā  (stokam antaraṃ gatvā) tapovananivāsinām uparodho mā bhūt / etāvaty eva rathaṃ sthāpaya yāvad avatarāmi /
children.translated_text: King: (Going a short distance) Let there be no disturbance to the forest-dwellers. Stop the chariot just here, so that I may descend.

children.text: rājā -- (stokam antaraṃ gatvā) tapo-vana-nivāsinām uparodho mā bhūt / etāvaty eva rathaṃ sthāpaya yāvad avatarāmi /
sūta  dhṛtāḥ pragrahāḥ / avataratv āyuṣmān /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: The reins are held. Let the long-lived one descend.

children.text: sūta -- dhṛtāḥ pragrahāḥ / avataratv āyuṣmān /

rājā  (avatīrya) sūta vinītaveṣeṇa praveṣṭavyāni tapovanāni nāma / idaṃ tāvad gṛhyatām / (iti sūtasyābharaṇāni dhanuś copanīyārpayati) sūta yāvad āśramavāsinaḥ pratyavekṣyāham upāvarte tāvad ārdrapṛṣṭhāḥ kriyantāṃ vājinaḥ /
children.translated_text: King: (Descending) Charioteer, one must enter ascetic groves in humble attire. Here, take these. (He hands over his ornaments and bow to the Charioteer.) Charioteer, while I go to visit the hermitage-dwellers and return, let the horses' backs be moistened [with water].

children.text: rājā -- (avatīrya) sūta vinīta-veṣeṇa praveṣṭavyāni tapo-vanāni nāma / idaṃ tāvad gṛhyatām / (iti sūtasyā abharaṇāni dhanuś ca upanīya arpayati) sūta yāvad āśrama-vāsinaḥ pratyavekṣya aham upāvarte tāvad ārdra-pṛṣṭhāḥ kriyantāṃ vājinaḥ /
sūta  tathā (iti niṣkrāntaḥ)
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>: So be it. (He exits.)

children.text: sūta -- tathā (iti niṣkrāntaḥ)
rājā  (parikramyāvalokya ca) idam āśramadvāram /yāvat praviśāmi (praviśya / nimittaṃ sūcayan)
children.translated_text: King: (Walking about and looking) Here is the hermitage gate. Let me enter. (Entering, and indicating an omen:)

children.text: rājā -- (parikramya avalokya ca) idam āśrama-dvāram /yāvat praviśāmi (praviśya / nimittaṃ sūcayan)
śāntam idam āśramapadaṃ sphurati ca bāhuḥ kutaḥ phalam ihāsya /
children.translated_text: This hermitage is peaceful, yet my arm throbs — what fruit can there be from this here?

children.text: athavā bhavitavyānāṃ dvārāṇi bhavanti sarvatra //
children.translated_text: But then, the gateways of destiny are found everywhere.

children.text: śāntam idam āśrama-padaṃ sphurati ca bāhuḥ kutaḥ phalam iha asya /
athavā bhavitavyānāṃ dvārāṇi bhavanti sarvatra //
(nepathye)
children.translated_text: (From behind the scenes:)

children.text: (nepathye)
ita itaḥ sakhyau /
children.translated_text: 'This way, this way, dear friends!'

children.text: ita itaḥ sakhyau /

rājā  (karṇaṃ dattvā) aye dakṣiṇena vṛkṣavāṭikām ālāpa iva śrūyate / yāvad atra gacchāmi / (parikramyāvalokya ca) aye etās tapasvikanyakāḥ svapramāṇānurūpaiḥ secanaghaṭair bālapādapebhyaḥ payo dātum ita evābhivartante (nipuṇaṃ nirūpya) aho madhuram āsāṃ darśanam /
children.translated_text: King: (Listening) Ah, to the right of the tree-garden, speech seems to be heard. Let me go there. (Walking about and looking) Ah, these are young hermit-maidens, coming this way to give water to the young trees with watering-pots suited to their own size. (Looking closely) Ah, how sweet is the sight of them!

children.text: rājā -- (karṇaṃ dattvā) aye dakṣiṇena vṛkṣa-vāṭikām ālāpa iva śrūyate / yāvad atra gacchāmi / (parikramya avalokya ca) aye etās tapasvi-kanyakāḥ sva-pramāṇa-anurūpaiḥ secana-ghaṭair bāla-pādapebhyaḥ payo dātum ita eva abhivartante (nipuṇaṃ nirūpya) aho madhuram āsāṃ darśanam /
śuddhāntadurlabham idaṃ vapur āśramavāsino yadi janasya /
children.translated_text: If such beauty of form is found even among the people dwelling in hermitages,

children.text: dūrīkṛtāḥ khalu guṇair udyānalatā vanalatābhiḥ //
children.translated_text: then truly the garden creepers are surpassed in their qualities by the forest creepers!

children.text: śuddha-anta-durlabham idaṃ vapur āśrama-vāsino yadi janasya /
dūrī-kṛtāḥ khalu guṇair udyāna-latā vana-latābhiḥ //
yāvad imāṃ chāyām āśritya pratipālayāmi (iti vilokayan sthitaḥ)
children.translated_text: I shall stand in this shade and wait. (He stands watching.)

children.text: yāvad imāṃ chāyām āśritya pratipālayāmi (iti vilokayan sthitaḥ)
śakuntalā  ita itaḥ sakhyau /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: 'This way, this way, dear friends!'

children.text: śakuntalā -- ita itaḥ sakhyau /
anasūyā  halā śakuntale tvatto 'pi tātakāśyapasyāśramavṛkṣakāḥ priyatareti tarkayāmi / yena navamālikākusumapelavā api tvam eteṣām ālavālapūraṇe niyuktā /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Dear <s>Śakuntalā</s>, I think the hermitage trees are dearer to father <s>Kāśyapa</s> even than you — since, delicate as you are [like] the young <s>navamālikā</s> (jasmine) blossoms, you are appointed to fill their tree-basins.

children.text: anasūyā -- halā śakuntale tvatto 'pi tāta-kāśyapasyā aśrama-vṛkṣakāḥ priyatara īti tarkayāmi / yena nava-mālikā-kusuma-pelavā api tvam eteṣām ālavāla-pūraṇe niyuktā /
śakuntalā  na kevalaṃ tātaniyoga eva / asti me sodarasneho 'py eteṣu / (iti vṛkṣasecanaṃ rūpayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: It is not merely father's appointment; I feel a sisterly affection for them too. (She mimes watering the trees.)

children.text: śakuntalā -- na kevalaṃ tāta-niyoga eva / asti me sodara-sneho 'py eteṣu / (iti vṛkṣa-secanaṃ rūpayati)
rājā  katham iyaṃ sā kaṇvaduhitā / asādhudarśī khalu tatrabhavān kāśyapo ya imām āśramadharme niyuṅkte /
children.translated_text: King: What! Is she <s>Kaṇva's</s> daughter? The venerable <s>Kāśyapa</s> is surely undiscerning, who assigns her to the duties of the hermitage.

children.text: rājā -- katham iyaṃ sā kaṇva-duhitā / asādhu-darśī khalu tatra-bhavān kāśyapo ya imām āśrama-dharme niyuṅkte /
idaṃ kilāvyājamanoharaṃ vapus tapaḥkṣamaṃ sādhayituṃ ya icchati /
children.translated_text: He who wishes to make this body — artlessly enchanting — fit for austerity,

children.text: dhruvaṃ sa nīlotpalapatradhārayā śamīlatāṃ chettum ṛṣir vyavasyati //
children.translated_text: that sage surely intends to cut a <s>śamī</s> (acacia) creeper with a blade of blue lotus petals!

children.text: idaṃ kila-avyāja-manoharaṃ vapus tapaḥ-kṣamaṃ sādhayituṃ ya icchati /
dhruvaṃ sa nīla-utpala-patra-dhārayā śamī-latāṃ chettum ṛṣir vyavasyati //
bhavatu / pādapāntarhita eva tāvad enāṃ paśyāmi / (iti tathā karoti)
children.translated_text: Well then, I shall observe her, concealed behind these trees. (He does so.)

children.text: bhavatu / pādapa-antarhita eva tāvad enāṃ paśyāmi / (iti tathā karoti)
śakuntalā  sakhi anasūye atipinaddhena valkalena priyaṃ vadayā niyantritāsmi / śithilaya tāvad etat /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: Friend <s>Anasūyā</s>, I have been bound too tightly by <s>Priyaṃvadā</s> with this bark-garment. Loosen it, please.

children.text: śakuntalā -- sakhi anasūye atipinaddhena valkalena priyaṃ vadayā niyantrita āsmi / śithilaya tāvad etat /
anasūyā  tathā / (iti śikhilayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Very well. (She loosens it.)

children.text: anasūyā -- tathā / (iti śikhilayati)
priyaṃvadā  (sahāsam) atra payodharavistārayitṛ ātmano yauvanam upālabhasva / māṃ kim upālabhase /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: (Laughing) Blame your own youth, which swells your bosom, for this — why blame me?

children.text: priyaṃvadā -- (sahāsam) atra payo-dhara-vistārayitṛ ātmano yauvanam upālabhasva / māṃ kim upālabhase /
rājā  kāmam ananurūpam asya vapuṣo valkalaṃ na punar alaṃkāraśriyaṃ na puṣyati / kutaḥ
children.translated_text: King: Indeed the bark-garment is ill-suited to her form, yet it does not fail to lend the beauty of ornament. How so?

children.text: rājā -- kāmam ananurūpam asya vapuṣo valkalaṃ na punar alaṃkāra-śriyaṃ na puṣyati / kutaḥ
sarasijam anuviddhaṃ śaivalenāpi ramyam
malinam api himāṃśor lakṣma lakṣmīṃ tanoti /
children.translated_text: a dark spot only enhances the beauty of the moon;
A lotus is lovely even when entangled with moss;

children.text: iyam adhikamanojñā valkalenāpi tanvī /
kim iva hi madhurāṇāṃ maṇḍanaṃ nākṛtīnām //
children.translated_text: for what indeed is not an adornment for beautiful forms?
this slender one is all the more enchanting even in bark-garment —

children.text: sarasijam anuviddhaṃ śaivalena api ramyam
malinam api hima-aṃśor lakṣma lakṣmīṃ tanoti /
iyam adhika-manojñā valkalena api tanvī /
kim iva hi madhurāṇāṃ maṇḍanaṃ nā akṛtīnām //
śakuntalā  (agrato 'valokya) eṣa vāteritapallavāṅgulībhis tvarayatīva+māṃ kesaravṛkṣakaḥ / yāvad enaṃ saṃbhāvayāmi (iti parikrāmati)
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (Looking ahead) This <s>kesara</s> (mango) sapling beckons me with its leaf-fingers stirred by the wind, as if urging me on. Let me attend to it. (She walks over.)

children.text: śakuntalā -- (agrato 'valokya) eṣa vāta-īrita-pallava-aṅgulībhis tvarayati iva+māṃ kesara-vṛkṣakaḥ / yāvad enaṃ saṃbhāvayāmi (iti parikrāmati)
priyaṃvadā  halā śakuntale atreva+tāvan muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha yāvat tvayopagatayā latāsanātha iva ayaṃ kesaravṛkṣakaḥ pratibhāti /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: Dear <s>Śakuntalā</s>, stand right there for just a moment — with you beside it, this <s>kesara</s> sapling appears as if a creeper has found its tree-lord.

children.text: priyaṃvadā -- halā śakuntale atra iva+tāvan muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha yāvat tvaya ūpagatayā latā-sanātha iva ayaṃ kesara-vṛkṣakaḥ pratibhāti /
ataḥ khalu priyaṃvadāsi tvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: That is precisely why you are named <s>Priyaṃvadā</s> ('Sweet-speaker')!

children.text: ataḥ khalu priyaṃvada āsi tvam /
rājā  priyam api tathyam āha śakuntalāṃ priyaṃvadā / asyāḥ khalu
children.translated_text: King: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s> speaks pleasingly to <s>Śakuntalā</s>, yet truly. For indeed —

children.text: rājā -- priyam api tathyam āha śakuntalāṃ priyaṃvadā / asyāḥ khalu
adharaḥ kisalayarāgaḥ komalaviṭapānukāriṇau bāhū /
children.translated_text: her lower lip has the color of a young leaf; her arms are [soft] like tender branches;

children.text: kusumam iva lobhanīyaṃ yauvanam aṅgeṣu saṃnaddham //
children.translated_text: her youth, alluring as a blossom, is arrayed upon her limbs.

children.text: adharaḥ kisalaya-rāgaḥ komala-viṭapa-anukāriṇau bāhū /
kusumam iva lobhanīyaṃ yauvanam aṅgeṣu saṃnaddham //
anasūyā  halā śakuntale iyaṃ svayaṃ varavadhūḥ sahakārasya tvayā kṛtanāmadheyā vanajyotsneti navamālikā / enāṃ vismṛtāsi /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Dear <s>Śakuntalā</s>, this <s>navamālikā</s> (jasmine) creeper, which you yourself named 'Forest Moonlight,' chosen as the bride of the mango tree — you have forgotten her!

children.text: anasūyā -- halā śakuntale iyaṃ svayaṃ vara-vadhūḥ saha-kārasya tvayā kṛta-nāmadheyā vana-jyotsna īti nava-mālikā / enāṃ vismṛta āsi /

śakuntalā  tad ātmānam api vismariṣyāmi / (latām upetyāvalokya ca) halā ramaṇīye khalu kāla etasya latāpādapamithunasya vyatikaraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / navakusumayauvanā vanajyotsnā snigdhapallavatayopabhogakṣamaḥ sahakāraḥ / (iti paśyantī tiṣṭhati)
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: Then I will forget even myself. (Approaching a creeper and looking at it) Dear friend, how lovely indeed is the season when this creeper-and-tree couple has come together! The <s>vanajyotsnā</s> (forest-moonlight jasmine) is in the bloom of fresh-flower youth, and the mango tree, with its tender sprouts, is fit for enjoyment. (Thus gazing, she stands.)

children.text: śakuntalā -- tad ātmānam api vismariṣyāmi / (latām upetya avalokya ca) halā ramaṇīye khalu kāla etasya latā-pādapa-mithunasya vyatikaraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / nava-kusuma-yauvanā vana-jyotsnā snigdha-pallavataya ūpabhoga-kṣamaḥ sahakāraḥ / (iti paśyantī tiṣṭhati)
priyaṃvadā  anasūye jānāsi kiṃ śakuntalā vanajyotsnām atimātraṃ paśyatīti /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: <s>Anasūyā</s>, do you know why <s>Śakuntalā</s> gazes so intently at the <s>vanajyotsnā</s>?

children.text: priyaṃvadā -- anasūye jānāsi kiṃ śakuntalā vana-jyotsnām atimātraṃ paśyati iti /
anasūyā  na khalu vibhāvayāmi / kathaya /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: I cannot imagine. Tell me.

children.text: anasūyā -- na khalu vibhāvayāmi / kathaya /
pri  yathā vanajyotsnānurūpeṇa pādapena saṃgatā api nāmaivam aham apy ātmano 'nurūpaṃ varaṃ labheyeti /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: 'Just as the <s>vanajyotsnā</s> has been united with a tree suited to her, may I too obtain a husband suited to myself!'

children.text: pri -- yathā vana-jyotsna ānurūpeṇa pādapena saṃgatā api nāma evam aham apy ātmano 'nurūpaṃ varaṃ labheya iti /
śaku  eṣa nūnaṃ tavātmagato manorathaḥ / (iti kalaśam āvarjayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: Surely this is a desire residing in your own heart! (She tilts the water-pitcher.)

children.text: śaku -- eṣa nūnaṃ tavā atma-gato manorathaḥ / (iti kalaśam āvarjayati)
rājā  api nāma kulapater iyam asavarṇakṣetrasaṃbhavā syāt / athavā kṛtaṃ saṃdehena
children.translated_text: The King: Could she perhaps be born from the patriarch's union with a woman of different <s>varṇa</s> (social class)? But enough of doubt—

children.text: rājā -- api nāma kula-pater iyam asavarṇa-kṣetra-saṃbhavā syāt / athavā kṛtaṃ saṃdehena
asaṃśayaṃ kṣatraparigrahakṣamā yad āryam asyām abhilāṣi me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Undoubtedly she is fit for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>'s embrace, for my noble mind desires her;

children.text: satāṃ hi saṃdehapadeṣu vastuṣu pramāṇam antaḥkaraṇa pravṛttayaḥ //
children.translated_text: for in matters where the virtuous have cause for doubt, the inclinations of the inner heart are the authority. //

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ kṣatra-parigraha-kṣamā yad āryam asyām abhilāṣi me manaḥ /
satāṃ hi saṃdeha-padeṣu vastuṣu pramāṇam antaḥ-karaṇa pravṛttayaḥ //
tathāpi tattvata enām upalabhye /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, I shall ascertain the truth about her.

children.text: tatha āpi tattvata enām upalabhye /
śaku  (sasaṃbhramam) ambho / salilasekasaṃbhramodgato navamālikām ujjhitvā vadanaṃ me madhukaro 'bhivartate (iti bhramarabādhāṃ rūpayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (Startled) Oh! A bee, disturbed by the agitation of my watering, has left the <s>navamālikā</s> (jasmine) and is heading for my face! (She mimes being harassed by a bee.)

children.text: śaku -- (sasaṃbhramam) ambho / salila-seka-saṃbhrama-udgato navamālikām ujjhitvā vadanaṃ me madhu-karo 'bhivartate (iti bhramara-bādhāṃ rūpayati)
rājā  (saspṛham)
children.translated_text: The King: (With longing)

children.text: rājā -- (saspṛham)
calāpāṅgāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ spṛśasi bahuśo vepathumatīm
rahasy ākhyāyīva+svanasi mṛdu karṇāntikacaraḥ /
children.translated_text: humming softly near her ear, as if whispering a secret;
You touch her glance, trembling, with darting sidelong looks again and again;

children.text: karau vyādhunvatyāḥ pibasi ratisarvasvam adharam
vayaṃ tattvānveṣān madhukara hatās tvaṃ khalu kṛtī //
children.translated_text: we are slain by our search for truth, O bee—it is you who are the successful one! //
you drink the nectar of her lower lip, the very essence of love's delight, while she waves her hands;

children.text: cala-apāṅgāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ spṛśasi bahuśo vepathumatīm
rahasy ākhyāyi īva+svanasi mṛdu karṇa-antika-caraḥ /
karau vyādhunvatyāḥ pibasi rati-sarvasvam adharam
vayaṃ tattva-anveṣān madhu-kara hatās tvaṃ khalu kṛtī //
na eṣa dhrṣṭo viramati / anyato gamiṣyāmi / katham ito 'py āgacchati / halā paritrāyethāṃ mām anena durvinītena madhukareṇābhibhūyamānām /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: This brazen one does not cease! I shall move elsewhere. What, it follows me here too! Dear friends, save me from this ill-mannered bee that harasses me!

children.text: na eṣa dhrṣṭo viramati / anyato gamiṣyāmi / katham ito 'py āgacchati / halā paritrāyethāṃ mām anena durvinītena madhu-kareṇa abhibhūyamānām /
ubhe  (sasmitam) ke āvāṃ paritrātum / duṣyaṃtam ākranda / rājarakṣitavyāni tapovanāni nāma /
children.translated_text: Both: (Smiling) Who are we to save you? Call upon <s>Duṣyanta</s>! For hermitages are under the king's protection.

children.text: ubhe -- (sasmitam) ke āvāṃ paritrātum / duṣyaṃtam ākranda / rāja-rakṣitavyāni tapo-vanāni nāma /
rājā  avasaro 'yam ātmānaṃ prakāśayitum / na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyam  (ity ardhokte svagatam) rājabhāvas tv abhijñāto bhavet / bhavatv evaṃ tāvad abhidhāsye /
children.translated_text: The King: This is the moment to reveal myself. 'Fear not, fear not—' (Breaking off, to himself) But then my kingly identity would be recognized. Very well, I shall speak thus nevertheless.

children.text: rājā -- avasaro 'yam ātmānaṃ prakāśayitum / na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyam -- (ity ardha-ukte svagatam) rāja-bhāvas tv abhijñāto bhavet / bhavatv evaṃ tāvad abhidhāsye /
śaku  (padāntare sthitvā /sadṛṣṭikṣepam) katham ito 'pi mām anusarati /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (Pausing mid-step, with a sidelong glance) How—it still pursues me here!

children.text: śaku -- (pada-antare sthitvā /sadṛṣṭi-kṣepam) katham ito 'pi mām anusarati /
rājā  (satvaram upasṛtya) āḥ
children.translated_text: The King: (Approaching swiftly) Ah!

children.text: rājā -- (satvaram upasṛtya) āḥ
kaḥ paurave vasumatīṃ śāsati śāsitari durvinītānām /
children.translated_text: When the ruler of the <s>Paurava</s> [dynasty] governs the earth, chastiser of the unruly,

children.text: ayam ācaraty avinayaṃ mugdhāsu tapasvikanyāsu //
children.translated_text: who commits this outrage against innocent ascetic maidens? //

children.text: kaḥ paurave vasumatīṃ śāsati śāsitari durvinītānām /
ayam ācaraty avinayaṃ mugdhāsu tapasvi-kanyāsu //
(sarvā rājānaṃ dṛṣṭā kiṃcid iva saṃbhrāntāḥ)
children.translated_text: (All, seeing the King, are somewhat startled.)

children.text: (sarvā rājānaṃ dṛṣṭā kiṃcid iva saṃbhrāntāḥ)
anasūyā  āryaṇ na khalu kim apy atyāhitam / iyaṃ nau priyasakhī madhukareṇābhibhūyamānā kātarībhūtā / (iti śakuntalāṃ darśayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Sir, nothing truly harmful has happened. This dear friend of ours was simply frightened by a bee harassing her. (She points to <s>Śakuntalā</s>.)

children.text: anasūyā -- āryaṇ na khalu kim apy atyāhitam / iyaṃ nau priya-sakhī madhu-kareṇa abhibhūyamānā kātarī-bhūtā / (iti śakuntalāṃ darśayati)
rājā  (śakuntalābhimukho bhūtvā) api tapo vardhate /
children.translated_text: The King: (Turning toward <s>Śakuntalā</s>) Does your penance flourish?

children.text: rājā -- (śakuntalā-abhimukho bhūtvā) api tapo vardhate /
(śakuntalā sādhvasād avacanā tiṣṭhati)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śakuntalā</s> stands silent with bashfulness.)

children.text: (śakuntalā sādhvasād avacanā tiṣṭhati)
anasūyā  idānīm atithiviśeṣalābhena / halā śakuntale gacchoṭajam / phalamiśram argham upahara / idaṃ pādodakaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Indeed it does, now that we have gained a distinguished guest. Dear <s>Śakuntalā</s>, go to the cottage. Bring an offering of fruits. This water will serve for washing the feet.

children.text: anasūyā -- idānīm atithi-viśeṣa-lābhena / halā śakuntale gaccha uṭajam / phala-miśram argham upahara / idaṃ pāda-udakaṃ bhaviṣyati /
rājā  bhavatīnāṃ sūnṛtayā eva kṛtam ātithyam /
children.translated_text: The King: The hospitality of your kind words is itself sufficient.

children.text: rājā -- bhavatīnāṃ sūnṛtayā eva kṛtam ātithyam /
priyaṃvadā  tena hy asyāṃ prachāyaśītalāyāṃ saptaparṇavedikāyāṃ muhūrtam upaviśya pariśramavinodaṃ karotv āryaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: Then let the noble sir sit for a moment on this <s>saptaparṇa</s> (seven-leaved tree) bench, cool with shade, and take rest from his fatigue.

children.text: priyaṃvadā -- tena hy asyāṃ prachāya-śītalāyāṃ sapta-parṇa-vedikāyāṃ muhūrtam upaviśya pariśrama-vinodaṃ karotv āryaḥ /
rājā  nūnaṃ yūyam apy anena karmaṇā pariśrāntāḥ /
children.translated_text: The King: Surely you too are wearied by your tasks.

children.text: rājā -- nūnaṃ yūyam apy anena karmaṇā pariśrāntāḥ /
anasūyā  halā śakuntale ucitaṃ naḥ paryupāsanam atithīnām / atropaviśāmaḥ (iti sarvā upaviśanti)
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Dear <s>Śakuntalā</s>, it is proper for us to attend upon our guests. Let us sit here. (All sit down.)

children.text: anasūyā -- halā śakuntale ucitaṃ naḥ paryupāsanam atithīnām / atra upaviśāmaḥ (iti sarvā upaviśanti)
śaku  (ātmagatam) kiṃ nu khalv imaṃ prekṣya tapovanavirodhino vikārasya gamanīyāsmi saṃvṛttā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (To herself) Why is it that upon seeing this man, I have come to feel an emotion contrary to the spirit of the hermitage?

children.text: śaku -- (ātma-gatam) kiṃ nu khalv imaṃ prekṣya tapo-vana-virodhino vikārasya gamanīya āsmi saṃvṛttā /
rājā  (sarvā vilokya) aho samavayorūparamaṇīyaṃ bhavatīnāṃ sauhārdam /
children.translated_text: The King: (Looking at all of them) Ah, how charming is the friendship among you—equally matched in age and beauty!

children.text: rājā -- (sarvā vilokya) aho sama-vayo-rūpa-ramaṇīyaṃ bhavatīnāṃ sauhārdam /
pri  (janāntikam) anasūye ko nu khalv eṣa caturagambhīrākṛtir madhuraṃ priyam ālapan prabhāvavān iva lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: (Aside) <s>Anasūyā</s>, who indeed is this person of handsome, dignified form, speaking sweetly and pleasantly, who appears to be one of great authority?

children.text: pri -- (jana-antikam) anasūye ko nu khalv eṣa catura-gambhīra-ākṛtir madhuraṃ priyam ālapan prabhāvavān iva lakṣyate /
ana  sakhi mama apy asti kautūhalam / pṛcchāmi tāvad enam
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Friend, I too am curious. I shall ask him.

children.text: ana -- sakhi mama apy asti kautūhalam / pṛcchāmi tāvad enam
(prakāśam)
children.translated_text: (Aloud)

children.text: (prakāśam)

āryasya madhurālāpajanito viśrambho māṃ mantrayate katama āryeṇa rājarṣivaṃśo 'laṃkriyate katamo vā virahaparyutsukajanaḥ kuto deśaḥ kiṃ nimittaṃ vā sukumārataro 'pi tapovanagamanapariśramasyātmā padam upanītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sir, the confidence born of your sweet speech emboldens me to ask: what royal-sage lineage does the noble sir adorn? What region is it whose people are afflicted with the sorrow of your absence? And for what reason has your person, though too delicate for such, been brought to endure the fatigue of visiting a hermitage?

children.text: āryasya madhura-ālāpa-janito viśrambho māṃ mantrayate katama āryeṇa rājarṣi-vaṃśo 'laṃkriyate katamo vā viraha-paryutsuka-janaḥ kuto deśaḥ kiṃ nimittaṃ vā sukumārataro 'pi tapo-vana-gamana-pariśramasyā atmā padam upanītaḥ /
śaku  (ātmagatam) hṛdaya mottāmya / eṣā tvayā cintitāny anasūyā mantrayate /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (To herself) O heart, do not be restless! <s>Anasūyā</s> is asking what you have been thinking!

children.text: śaku -- (ātma-gatam) hṛdaya ma ūttāmya / eṣā tvayā cintitāny anasūyā mantrayate /

rājā  (ātmagatam) katham idānīm ātmānaṃ nivedayāmi kathaṃ vātmāpahāraṃ karomi / bhavatu / evaṃ tāvad enāṃ vakṣye / (prakāśam) bhavati yaḥ pauraveṇa rājñā dharmādhikāre niyuktaḥ so 'ham avighnakriyopalambhāya dharmāraṇyam idam āyātaḥ /
children.translated_text: The King: (To himself) How shall I now introduce myself, and how shall I conceal myself? Very well, I shall speak to her thus. (Aloud) Lady, I am the one appointed by the <s>Paurava</s> king to oversee the administration of <s>dharma</s>; I have come to this sacred forest to ensure that the religious observances proceed without obstruction.

children.text: rājā --- (ātma-gatam) katham idānīm ātmānaṃ nivedayāmi kathaṃ vā ātma-apahāraṃ karomi / bhavatu / evaṃ tāvad enāṃ vakṣye / (prakāśam) bhavati yaḥ pauraveṇa rājñā dharma-adhikāre niyuktaḥ so 'ham avighna-kriyā-upalambhāya dharma-araṇyam idam āyātaḥ /
(śakuntalā śṛṅgāralajjāṃ rūpayati)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śakuntalā</s> displays amorous bashfulness.)

children.text: (śakuntalā śṛṅgāra-lajjāṃ rūpayati)
ana  (ubhayor ākāraṃ viditvā / janāntikam) halā śakuntale yad yatrādya tātaḥ saṃnihito bhavet /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: (Perceiving the bearing of both; aside) Dear <s>Śakuntalā</s>, if only father were present here today!

children.text: ana -- (ubhayor ākāraṃ viditvā / jana-antikam) halā śakuntale yad yatra adya tātaḥ saṃnihito bhavet /
śaku  tataḥ kiṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: Then what would happen?

children.text: śaku -- tataḥ kiṃ bhavet /
sakhyau  imaṃ jīvitasarvasvenāpy atithiviśeṣaṃ kṛtārthaṃ kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: Both friends: He would fulfill this distinguished guest's every wish, even with his very life!

children.text: sakhyau -- imaṃ jīvita-sarvasvena apy atithi-viśeṣaṃ kṛta-arthaṃ kariṣyati /
śaku  yuvām apetam / kim api hṛdaye kṛtvā matrayethe / na yuvayor vacanaṃ śroṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: Be off with you both! You are concocting something in your hearts. I shall not listen to your words.

children.text: śaku -- yuvām apetam / kim api hṛdaye kṛtvā matrayethe / na yuvayor vacanaṃ śroṣyāmi /
rājā  vayam api tāvad bhavatyoḥ sakhīgataṃ kim api pṛcchāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: The King: We too would like to ask your friends about something.

children.text: rājā -- vayam api tāvad bhavatyoḥ sakhī-gataṃ kim api pṛcchāmaḥ /
sakkyau  ārya anugraha iveyam abhyarthanā /
children.translated_text: Both friends: Sir, this request is like a favor.

children.text: sakkyau -- ārya anugraha iva iyam abhyarthanā /
rājā  bhagavān kāśyapaḥ śāśvate brahmaṇi sthita iti prakāśaḥ / iyaṃ ca vaḥ sakhī tad ātmajeti katham etat /
children.translated_text: The King: The revered <s>Kāśyapa</s> is renowned as one established in the eternal <s>Brahman</s>. And this friend of yours is said to be his daughter—how is this?

children.text: rājā -- bhagavān kāśyapaḥ śāśvate brahmaṇi sthita iti prakāśaḥ / iyaṃ ca vaḥ sakhī tad ātmaja īti katham etat /
anasūyā  śṛṇotv āryaḥ / asti ko 'pi kauśika iti gotranāmadheyo mahāprabhāvo rājarṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Let the noble sir hear. There is a certain royal sage of great power, known by the clan-name <s>Kauśika</s> (Viśvāmitra).

children.text: anasūyā -- śṛṇotv āryaḥ / asti ko 'pi kauśika iti gotra-nāma-dheyo mahā-prabhāvo rājarṣiḥ /
rājā  asti / śrūyate /
children.translated_text: The King: Indeed, so it is heard.

children.text: rājā -- asti / śrūyate /
ana  tam āvayoḥ priyasakhyāḥ prabhavam avagaccha / ujjhitāyāḥ śarīrasaṃvardhanādibhis tātakāśyapo 'syāḥ pitā /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Know him to be the progenitor of our dear friend. Having been abandoned [by her mother], Father <s>Kāśyapa</s> became her father by nurturing her body and the rest.

children.text: ana -- tam āvayoḥ priya-sakhyāḥ prabhavam avagaccha / ujjhitāyāḥ śarīra-saṃvardhana-ādibhis tāta-kāśyapo 'syāḥ pitā /
rājā  ujjhitaśabdena janitaṃ me kautūhalam / āmūlāt+śrotum icchāmi /
children.translated_text: The King: The word 'abandoned' arouses my curiosity. I wish to hear from the beginning.

children.text: rājā -- ujjhita-śabdena janitaṃ me kautūhalam / ā-mūlāt+śrotum icchāmi /
ana  śṛṇotv āryaḥ / gautamītīre purā kila tasya rājarṣer ugre tapasi vartamānasya kim api jātaśaṅkair devair menakā nāmāpsarāḥ preṣitā niyamavighnakāriṇī /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Let the noble sir hear. Once upon a time, on the bank of the <s>Gautamī</s> (Godāvarī), while that royal sage was engaged in fierce austerities, the gods, becoming apprehensive about something, sent an <s>apsaras</s> named <s>Menakā</s> to obstruct his disciplines.

children.text: ana -- śṛṇotv āryaḥ / gautamī-tīre purā kila tasya rājarṣer ugre tapasi vartamānasya kim api jāta-śaṅkair devair menakā nāma-apsarāḥ preṣitā niyama-vighna-kāriṇī /
rājā  asty etad anyasamādhibhīrutvaṃ devānām /
children.translated_text: The King: Indeed, this fear of others' concentrated meditation is [characteristic] of the gods.

children.text: rājā -- asty etad anya-samādhi-bhīrutvaṃ devānām /
anasūyā  tato vasantodārasamaye tasyā unmādayitṛ rūpaṃ prekṣya  (ity ardhokte lajjayā viramati)
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Then, in the generous season of spring, seeing her beauty that could drive one mad— (Breaking off midway, she stops from modesty.)

children.text: anasūyā -- tato vasanta-udāra-samaye tasyā unmādayitṛ rūpaṃ prekṣya -- (ity ardha-ukte lajjayā viramati)
rājā  parastāj jñāyata eva / sarvathāpsaraḥsaṃbhavaiṣā /
children.translated_text: The King: The rest is understood. In every way, she is of celestial birth.

children.text: rājā -- parastāj jñāyata eva / sarvatha āpsaraḥ-saṃbhava aiṣā /
anasūyā  atha kim /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Indeed, what else?

children.text: anasūyā -- atha kim /
rājā  upapadye /
children.translated_text: The King: It is fitting.

children.text: rājā -- upapadye /
mānuṣīṣu kathaṃ vā syād asya rūpasya saṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: How could this form have its origin among mortal women?

children.text: na prabhātaralaṃ jyotir udeti vasudhātalāt //
children.translated_text: The trembling dawn-light does not rise from the surface of the earth. //

children.text: mānuṣīṣu kathaṃ vā syād asya rūpasya saṃbhavaḥ /
na prabhā-taralaṃ jyotir udeti vasudhā-talāt //
(śakuntalādhomukhī tiṣṭhati)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śakuntalā</s> stands with face downcast.)

children.text: (śakuntala ādho-mukhī tiṣṭhati)
rājā  (ātmagatam) labdhāvakāśo me manorathaḥ / kiṃ tu sakhyā parihāsodāhṛtāṃ varaprārthanāṃ śrutvā dhṛtadvaidhībhāvakātaraṃ me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The King: (To himself) My heart's desire has found its opening! And yet, having heard the friend's jest about wishing for a husband, my mind is anxious, wavering between two alternatives.

children.text: rājā -- (ātma-gatam) labdha-avakāśo me mano-rathaḥ / kiṃ tu sakhyā parihāsa-udāhṛtāṃ vara-prārthanāṃ śrutvā dhṛta-dvaidhī-bhāva-kātaraṃ me manaḥ /
pri  (sasmitaṃ śakuntalāṃ vilokya nāyakābhimukhī bhūtvā)
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: (Looking at <s>Śakuntalā</s> with a smile, then turning toward the hero)

children.text: pri -- (sasmitaṃ śakuntalāṃ vilokya nāyaka-abhimukhī bhūtvā)
punar api vaktukāma ivāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: The noble sir seems as if he wishes to say something more.

children.text: punar api vaktu-kāma ivā aryaḥ /
(śakuntalāṃ sakhīm aṅgulyā tarjayati)
children.translated_text: (She wags her finger threateningly at <s>Śakuntalā</s>.)

children.text: (śakuntalāṃ sakhīm aṅgulyā tarjayati)
rājā  samyag upalakṣitaṃ bhavatyā / asti naḥ saccaritaśravaṇalobhād anyad api praṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: The King: You have observed correctly. Out of eagerness to hear of noble deeds, I have something further to ask.

children.text: rājā -- samyag upalakṣitaṃ bhavatyā / asti naḥ sac-carita-śravaṇa-lobhād anyad api praṣṭavyam /
pri  alaṃ vicārya / aniyantraṇānuyogas tapasvijano nāma /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: Do not hesitate. Ascetic folk are subject to unrestricted inquiry.

children.text: pri -- alaṃ vicārya / aniyantraṇa-anuyogas tapasvi-jano nāma /
rājā  it sakhīṃ te jñātum icchāmi /
children.translated_text: The King: I wish to know about your friend:

children.text: rājā -- it sakhīṃ te jñātum icchāmi /
vaikhānasaṃ kim anayā vratam āpradānād
vyāpārarodhi madanasya niṣevitavyam /
children.translated_text: thus obstructing the activities of <s>Madana</s> (the God of Love)?
Will this <s>vaikhānasa</s> (hermit) vow be observed by her until the giving-away [in marriage],

children.text: atyantam ātmasadṛśekṣaṇavallabhābhir
āho nivatsyati sama hariṇāṅganābhi //
children.translated_text: whose glances match her own, among the deer-maidens? //
Or will she dwell forever with the doe-eyed ones,

children.text: vaikhānasaṃ kim anayā vratam ā-pradānād
vyāpāra-rodhi madanasya niṣevitavyam /
atyantam ātma-sadṛśa-īkṣaṇa-vallabhābhir
āho nivatsyati sama hariṇa-aṅganābhi //
pri  ārya dharmacaraṇe 'pi paravaśo 'yaṃ janaḥ / guroḥ punar asyā anurūpavarapradāne saṃkalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: Sir, though she is indeed subject to others in her religious observances, her guardian has the intention of bestowing her upon a suitable husband.

children.text: pri -- ārya dharma-caraṇe 'pi para-vaśo 'yaṃ janaḥ / guroḥ punar asyā anurūpa-vara-pradāne saṃkalpaḥ /
rājā  (ātmagatam) an duravāpeyaṃ khalu prārthanā /
children.translated_text: The King: (To himself) Ah, this aspiration is not hard to attain!

children.text: rājā -- (ātma-gatam) an duravāpa īyaṃ khalu prārthanā /
bhava hṛdaya sābhilāṣaṃ saṃprati saṃdeha nirṇayo jātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Be hopeful, O heart! Now the resolution of doubt has come;

children.text: āśaṅkase yad agniṃ tad idaṃ sparśakṣamaṃ ratnam //
children.translated_text: what you feared was fire, that very thing is a gem fit to be touched. //

children.text: bhava hṛdaya sābhilāṣaṃ saṃprati saṃdeha nirṇayo jātaḥ /
āśaṅkase yad agniṃ tad idaṃ sparśa-kṣamaṃ ratnam //
śaku  (saroṣam iva) anasūye gamiṣyāmy aham /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (As if angry) <s>Anasūyā</s>, I am leaving!

children.text: śaku -- (saroṣam iva) anasūye gamiṣyāmy aham /
ana  kiṃ nimittam /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: For what reason?

children.text: ana -- kiṃ nimittam /
śaku  imām asaṃbaddhapralāpīṃ priyaṃvadām āryāyai gautamyai nivedayiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: I shall report this <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>, who talks irrelevant nonsense, to the Lady <s>Gautamī</s>!

children.text: śaku -- imām asaṃbaddha-pralāpīṃ priyaṃvadām āryāyai gautamyai nivedayiṣyāmi /
ana  sakhi na yuktam akṛtasatkāram atithiviśeṣaṃ visṛjya svachandato gamanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>: Friend, it is not proper to leave a distinguished guest without showing proper courtesy, going as you please.

children.text: ana -- sakhi na yuktam akṛta-satkāram atithi-viśeṣaṃ visṛjya svachandato gamanam /
(śakuntalā na kiṃcid uktvā prasthitaiva)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śakuntalā</s> proceeds to leave without saying anything.)

children.text: (śakuntalā na kiṃcid uktvā prasthita aiva)
rājā  (grahītum icchan nigṛhyātmānam / ātmagatam) aho ceṣṭā+pratirūpikā kāmijanamanovṛttiḥ / ahaṃ hi
children.translated_text: The King: (Wishing to seize [her], but restraining himself; to himself) Ah, the behavior of a lover's mind is true to its image! For I,

children.text: rājā -- (grahītum icchan nigṛhyā atmānam / ātma-gatam) aho ceṣṭā+pratirūpikā kāmi-jana-mano-vṛttiḥ / ahaṃ hi
anuyāsyan munitanayāṃ sahasā vinayena vāritaprasaraḥ /
children.translated_text: about to follow the sage's daughter, but suddenly checked by decorum,

children.text: sthānād anuccalann api gatveva+punaḥ pratinivṛttaḥ //
children.translated_text: without moving from my place, have gone and returned again, as it were. //

children.text: anuyāsyan muni-tanayāṃ sahasā vinayena vārita-prasaraḥ /
sthānād anuccalann api gatva īva+punaḥ pratinivṛttaḥ //
pri  (śakuntalāṃ nirudhya) halā na te yuktaṃ gantum /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: (Stopping <s>Śakuntalā</s>) Dear, it is not right for you to go.

children.text: pri -- (śakuntalāṃ nirudhya) halā na te yuktaṃ gantum /
śaku  (sabhrūbhaṅgam) kiṃ nimittam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (With a frown) Why not?

children.text: śaku -- (sabhrū-bhaṅgam) kiṃ nimittam /
pri  vṛkṣasecane dve dārayasi me / ehi tāvat / ātmānaṃ mocayitvā tato gamiṣyasi (iti balād enāṃ nivartayati)
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: You owe me two tree-waterings! Come, free yourself [from the debt] first, then you may go. (She forcibly turns her back.)

children.text: pri -- vṛkṣa-secane dve dārayasi me / ehi tāvat / ātmānaṃ mocayitvā tato gamiṣyasi (iti balād enāṃ nivartayati)
rājā  bhadre vṛkṣasecanād eva pariśrāntām atrabhavatīṃ lakṣaye / tathā hy asyāḥ
children.translated_text: The King: Good lady, I can see that this lady is fatigued from the very watering of trees. For indeed,

children.text: rājā -- bhadre vṛkṣa-secanād eva pariśrāntām atra-bhavatīṃ lakṣaye / tathā hy asyāḥ
srastāṃsāv atimātralohitatalau bāhū ghaṭotkṣepaṇād adya api stanavepathuṃ janayati śvāsaḥ pramāṇādhikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Her arms, with drooping shoulders and excessively reddened palms, [weary] from lifting the water-pots; her breath, exceeding its measure, even now causing a tremor in her breasts;

children.text: baddhaṃ karṇaśirīṣarodhi vadane dharmāmbhasāṃ jālakaṃ bandhe sraṃsini caikahastayamitāḥ paryākulā mūrdhajāḥ //
children.translated_text: the net of perspiration bound upon her face, obstructing the <s>śirīṣa</s> (silk-cotton) flower at her ear; and her hair, held by one hand, in disarray, its tie loosening. //

children.text: srasta-aṃsāv atimātra-lohita-talau bāhū ghaṭa-utkṣepaṇād adya api stana-vepathuṃ janayati śvāsaḥ pramāṇa-adhikaḥ /
baddhaṃ karṇa-śirīṣa-rodhi vadane dharma-ambhasāṃ jālakaṃ bandhe sraṃsini ca eka-hasta-yamitāḥ paryākulā mūrdhajāḥ //
tad aham enām anṛṇāṃ karomi (iti aṅgulīyaṃ dātum icchati)
children.translated_text: So let me discharge her debt. (He wishes to give the ring.)

children.text: tad aham enām anṛṇāṃ karomi (iti aṅgulīyaṃ dātum icchati)
(ubhe nāmamudrākṣarāṇy anuvācya parasparam avalokayataḥ)
children.translated_text: (Both, reading the letters of the name-seal, look at each other.)

children.text: (ubhe nāma-mudrā-akṣarāṇy anuvācya parasparam avalokayataḥ)
rājā  alam asmān anyathā saṃbhāvya / rājñaḥ parigraho 'yam iti rājapuruṣaṃ mām avagacchatha /
children.translated_text: The King: Do not think otherwise of me. This is the property of the king; know me simply as a royal officer.

children.text: rājā -- alam asmān anyathā saṃbhāvya / rājñaḥ parigraho 'yam iti rāja-puruṣaṃ mām avagacchatha /
pri  tena hi nārhaty aṅgulīyakam aṅgulīviyogam / āryasya vacanenānṛṇedānīm eṣā / (kiṃcid vihasya) halā śakuntale mocitāsy anukampināryeṇa / athavā mahārājena / gacchedānīm /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>: Then the ring should not suffer the separation from the finger. By the noble sir's word, she is now free of debt. (With a slight laugh) Dear <s>Śakuntalā</s>, you are freed by the compassionate noble sir—or rather, by the great king! Go now.

children.text: pri -- tena hi na arhaty aṅgulīyakam aṅgulī-viyogam / āryasya vacanena anṛṇa īdānīm eṣā / (kiṃcid vihasya) halā śakuntale mocita āsy anukampinā āryeṇa / athavā mahā-rājena / gaccha idānīm /
śaku  (ātmagatam) yady ātmanaḥ prabhaviṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: (To herself) If only I were mistress of myself!

children.text: śaku -- (ātma-gatam) yady ātmanaḥ prabhaviṣyāmi /
(prakāśam) kā tvaṃ visraṣṭavyasya roddhavyasya vā /
children.translated_text: (Aloud) Who are you to decide whether I should stay or go?

children.text: (prakāśam) kā tvaṃ visraṣṭavyasya roddhavyasya vā /
rājā  (śakuntalāṃ vilokya / ātmagatam) kiṃ nu khalu yathā vayam asyām evam iyam apy asmān prati syāt / athavā labdhāvakāśā me prārthanā / kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: The King: (Looking at <s>Śakuntalā</s>; to himself) Could it be that, just as we feel toward her, she too feels toward us? Or has my desire found its opening? Because—

children.text: rājā -- (śakuntalāṃ vilokya / ātma-gatam) kiṃ nu khalu yathā vayam asyām evam iyam apy asmān prati syāt / athavā labdha avakāśā me prārthanā / kutaḥ /
vācaṃ na miśrayati yady api madvacobhiḥ
karṇaṃ dadāty abhimukhaṃ mayi bhāṣamāṇe /
children.translated_text: she lends her ear attentively when I speak;
Though she does not mingle her words with mine,

children.text: kāmaṃ na tiṣṭhati madānanasaṃmukhīnām
bhūyiṣṭham anyaviṣayā na tu dṛṣṭir asyāḥ //
children.translated_text: her gaze, for the most part, is not directed elsewhere. //
though she does not remain face-to-face with me,

children.text: vācaṃ na miśrayati yady api mad-vacobhiḥ
karṇaṃ dadāty abhimukhaṃ mayi bhāṣamāṇe /
kāmaṃ na tiṣṭhati mada-ānana-saṃmukhīnām
bhūyiṣṭham anya-viṣayā na tu dṛṣṭir asyāḥ //
(nepathye)
children.translated_text: (Offstage)

children.text: (nepathye)
bho bhos tapasvinaḥ saṃnihitās tapovanasattvarakṣāyai bhavata / pratyāsannaḥ kila mṛga yā vihārī pārthivo duṣyantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Ho there, ascetics! Be at hand for the protection of the hermitage creatures! King <s>Duṣyanta</s>, the hunter of wild game, is reported to be nearby.

children.text: bho bhos tapasvinaḥ saṃnihitās tapo-vana-sattva-rakṣāyai bhavata / pratyāsannaḥ kila mṛga yā vihārī pārthivo duṣyantaḥ /
turagakhurahatas tathā hi reṇur viṭapaviṣaktajalārdravalkaleṣu /
children.translated_text: For dust, struck up by the hooves of horses, on the tree-branches with their wet-barked water-moistened [coverings],

children.text: patati pariṇatāruṇaprakāśaḥ śalabhasamūha ivāśramadrumeṣu //
children.translated_text: falls glowing with the color of ripe [evening] red, like a swarm of locusts upon the hermitage trees. //

children.text: turaga-khura-hatas tathā hi reṇur viṭapa-viṣakta-jala-ārdra-valkaleṣu /
patati pariṇata-aruṇa-prakāśaḥ śalabha-samūha ivā aśrama-drumeṣu //
api ca /
children.translated_text: And moreover—

children.text: api ca /
tīvrāghātapratihatataruskandhalagnaikadantaḥ
pādākṛṣṭavratativalayāsaṅgasaṃjātapāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: with a snare formed from the entanglement of trailing creeper-garlands caught by its feet;
With a single tusk lodged in a tree-trunk, struck by a violent blow;

children.text: mūrto vighnas tapasa iva no bhinnasāraṅgayūtho
dharmāraṇyaṃ praviśati gajaḥ syandanālokabhītaḥ //
children.translated_text: enters the sacred forest, frightened by the sight of a chariot. //
like an embodied obstacle to our penance, an elephant, whose herd of spotted deer has been scattered,

children.text: tīvra-āghāta-pratihata-taru-skandha-lagna-eka-dantaḥ
pāda-ākṛṣṭa-vratati-valayā-saṅga-saṃjāta-pāśaḥ /
mūrto vighnas tapasa iva no bhinna-sāraṅga-yūtho
dharma-araṇyaṃ praviśati gajaḥ syandana-āloka-bhītaḥ //
(sarvāḥ karṇaṃ dattvā kiṃcid iva saṃbhrāntāḥ)
children.translated_text: (All listen and become somewhat startled.)

children.text: (sarvāḥ karṇaṃ dattvā kiṃcid iva saṃbhrāntāḥ)
rājā  (ātmagatam) aho dhik paurā asmadanveṣiṇas tapovanam uparundhanti / bhavatu / pratigamiṣyāmas tāvat /
children.translated_text: The King: (To himself) Alas! My attendants, searching for me, are disturbing the hermitage! Very well, I shall go back.

children.text: rājā -- (ātma-gatam) aho dhik paurā asmad-anveṣiṇas tapo-vanam uparundhanti / bhavatu / pratigamiṣyāmas tāvat /
sakhyau  ārya anenāraṇyakavṛttāntena paryākulāḥ smaḥ / anujānīhi na uṭajagamanāya /
children.translated_text: Both friends: Sir, we are alarmed by this report of wild events. Permit us to return to the cottage.

children.text: sakhyau -- ārya anenā araṇyaka-vṛtta-antena paryākulāḥ smaḥ / anujānīhi na uṭaja-gamanāya /
rājā  (sasaṃbhramam) gacchantu bhavatyaḥ / vayam apy āśramapīḍā yathā na bhavati tathā prayatiṣyāmahe /
children.translated_text: The King: (With agitation) Go, ladies. And we too shall endeavor that no disturbance befalls the hermitage.

children.text: rājā -- (sasaṃbhramam) gacchantu bhavatyaḥ / vayam apy āśrama-pīḍā yathā na bhavati tathā prayatiṣyāmahe /
(sarve uttiṣṭhanti)
children.translated_text: (All rise.)

children.text: (sarve uttiṣṭhanti)
sakhyau  ārya asaṃbhāvitātithisatkāraṃ bhūyo 'pi prekṣaṇanimittaṃ lajjāmahe āryaṃ vijñāpayitum /
children.translated_text: Friends: Noble sir, we are embarrassed to invite you again for an audience, as we have been unable to offer proper hospitality to an unexpected guest.

children.text: sakhyau -- ārya asaṃbhāvita-atithi-satkāraṃ bhūyo 'pi prekṣaṇa-nimittaṃ lajjāmahe āryaṃ vijñāpayitum /
rājā  mā maivam / darśanenaiva bhavatīnāṃ puraskṛto 'smi /
children.translated_text: King: Please do not say so. I have been honored simply by the sight of you.

children.text: rājā -- mā ma aivam / darśanena eva bhavatīnāṃ puraskṛto 'smi /
śaku anasūye abhinavakuśasūcyā parīkṣataṃ caraṇaṃ kurabakaśākhāparilagnaṃ ca valkalam / tāvat paripālayata māṃ yāvad etan mocayāmi /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s>: <s>Anasūyā</s>, my foot is pricked by a fresh <s>kuśa</s>-grass tip, and my bark garment is caught on a <s>kurabaka</s> branch. Wait for me while I free it.

children.text: śaku-- anasūye abhinava-kuśa-sūcyā parīkṣataṃ caraṇaṃ kurabaka-śākhā-parilagnaṃ ca valkalam / tāvat paripālayata māṃ yāvad etan mocayāmi /
(śakuntalā rājānam avalokayantī savyājaṃ vilambya saha sakhībhyāṃ niṣkrāntā)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śakuntalā</s>, looking at the king with a feigned excuse for lingering, exits with her two friends.)

children.text: (śakuntalā rājānam avalokayantī savyājaṃ vilambya saha sakhībhyāṃ niṣkrāntā)
rājā  mandautsukyo 'smi nagaragamanaṃ prati / yāvad anuyātrikān sametya nātidūre tapovanasya niveśayeyam / na khalu śaknomi śakuntalāvyāpārād ātmānaṃ nivartayitum / mama hi
children.translated_text: King: My eagerness for returning to the city has diminished. Let me gather my retinue and encamp them not too far from the hermitage. Indeed, I cannot turn myself away from thoughts of <s>Śakuntalā</s>. For—

children.text: rājā -- manda-autsukyo 'smi nagara-gamanaṃ prati / yāvad anuyātrikān sametya na atidūre tapo-vanasya niveśayeyam / na khalu śaknomi śakuntalā-vyāpārād ātmānaṃ nivartayitum / mama hi
gacchati puraḥ śarīraṃ dhāvati paścād asaṃstutaṃ cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: My body moves forward, but my unacquainted heart runs back,

children.text: cīnāṃśukam iva ketoḥ prativātaṃ nīyamānasya //
children.translated_text: like the silk banner of a standard being carried against the wind.

children.text: gacchati puraḥ śarīraṃ dhāvati paścād asaṃstutaṃ cetaḥ /
cīna-aṃśukam iva ketoḥ prativātaṃ nīyamānasya //
(iti niṣkrāntāḥ sarve)
children.translated_text: (Thus all exit.)

children.text: (iti niṣkrāntāḥ sarve)
(prathamo 'ṅkaḥ)
children.translated_text: (End of Act One.)

children.text: dvitīyo 'ṅkaḥ
children.translated_text: Act Two

children.text: (tataha praviśati viṣaṇṇo vidūṣakaḥ)
children.translated_text: (Then enters the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>, looking dejected.)

children.text: (tataha praviśati viṣaṇṇo vidūṣakaḥ)

vidūṣaka  (niḥśvasya) bho disṭam / etasya mṛgayāśīlasya rājño vayasyabhāvena nirviṇṇo 'smi / ayaṃ mṛgo 'yaṃ vahāro 'yaṃ śārdūla iti madhyāhne 'pi grīṣmaviralapādapachāyāsu vanarājiṣv āhiṇḍayate aṭatīto 'ṭavī / patrasaṃkarakaṣāyāṇi kaduṣṇāni girinadījalāni pīyante / aniyatavelaṃ śūlyamāṃsabhūyiṣṭha āhāro bhujyate / turagānudhāvanakaṇḍitasaṃdhe rātrāv api nikāmaṃ śayitavyaṃ nāsti / tato mahaty eva pratyūṣe dāsyāḥ putraiḥ śakunilubdhakair vanagrahaṇakolāhalena pratibodhito 'smi / iyatedānīm api pīḍā na kiṣkrāmati / tato gaṇḍasyopari piṇḍakaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / hyaḥ kilāsmāsv avahīneṣu tatra bhavato mṛgānusāreṇāśramapadaṃ praviṣṭasya tāpasakanyakā śakuntalā mamādhanyatayā darśitā / sāṃprataṃ nagaragamanāya manaḥ katham api na karoti / adya api tasya tām eva cintayato 'kṣṇoḥ prabhātam āsīt / kā gatiḥ / yāvat taṃ kṛtācāraparikramaṃ paśyāmi / (iti parikramyāvalokya ca)
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Sighing) Oh, fate! I am utterly wearied by this friendship with the hunting-obsessed king. "This is a deer, this is a boar, this is a tiger"—even at midday in the sparse shade of summer trees, he drags me wandering through the forest tracks. We drink the lukewarm waters of mountain streams, bitter with the mixture of leaves. Food is eaten at irregular hours, consisting mostly of spit-roasted meat. At night, my joints shattered from chasing horses, there is no sleeping comfortably. Then at the crack of dawn I am awakened by the commotion of the bird-hunters, those sons of slaves, catching birds. And now even this torment does not end. For on top of it all, a boil has formed on my cheek. Yesterday, it seems, while we were left behind, that venerable one, following a deer's trail, entered a hermitage, and there, to my misfortune, a hermit's daughter named <s>Śakuntalā</s> was shown to him. Now his mind simply will not turn to going back to the city. Even today, his dawn has broken while he thinks only of her. What is to be done? Let me go see him after he has finished his morning rituals. (Walking around and looking)

children.text: vidūṣaka -- (niḥśvasya) bho disṭam / etasya mṛgayā-śīlasya rājño vayasya-bhāvena nirviṇṇo 'smi / ayaṃ mṛgo 'yaṃ vahāro 'yaṃ śārdūla iti madhya-ahne 'pi grīṣma-virala-pādapa-chāyāsu vana-rājiṣv āhiṇḍayate aṭatīto 'ṭavī / patra-saṃkara-kaṣāyāṇi kaduṣṇāni giri-nadī-jalāni pīyante / aniyata-velaṃ śūlya-māṃsa-bhūyiṣṭha āhāro bhujyate / turaga-anudhāvana-kaṇḍita-saṃdhe rātrāv api nikāmaṃ śayitavyaṃ na asti / tato mahaty eva pratyūṣe dāsyāḥ putraiḥ śakuni-lubdhakair vana-grahaṇa-kolāhalena pratibodhito 'smi / iyata īdānīm api pīḍā na kiṣkrāmati / tato gaṇḍasya upari piṇḍakaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / hyaḥ kila asmāsv avahīneṣu tatra bhavato mṛga-anusāreṇā aśrama-padaṃ praviṣṭasya tāpasa-kanyakā śakuntalā mama adhanyatayā darśitā / sāṃprataṃ nagara-gamanāya manaḥ katham api na karoti / adya api tasya tām eva cintayato 'kṣṇoḥ prabhātam āsīt / kā gatiḥ / yāvat taṃ kṛta-ācāra-parikramaṃ paśyāmi / (iti parikramya avalokya ca)

eṣa bāṇāsanahastābhir yavanībhir vanapuṣpamālādhāriṇībhiḥ parivṛta ita evāgachati priyavayasyaḥ / bhavatu / aṅgabhaṅgavikala iva bhūtvā sthāsyāmi / yady evam api nāma viśramaṃ labheya / (iti daṇḍakāṣṭham avalambya sthitaḥ)
(tataḥ praviśati yathānirdiṣṭaparivāro rājā)
children.translated_text: Here comes my dear friend, surrounded by <s>Yavanī</s> attendants with bows and arrows in hand, wearing garlands of wild flowers. Well then! I shall stand as if crippled in all my limbs. Perhaps in that way I might obtain some rest. (Standing leaning on a stick.) (Then enters the king with the retinue described.)

children.text:
eṣa bāṇa-āsana-hastābhir yavanībhir vana-puṣpa-mālā-dhāriṇībhiḥ parivṛta ita evā agachati priya-vayasyaḥ / bhavatu / aṅga-bhaṅga-vikala iva bhūtvā sthāsyāmi / yady evam api nāma viśramaṃ labheya / (iti daṇḍa-kāṣṭham avalambya sthitaḥ)
(tataḥ praviśati yathā-nirdiṣṭa-parivāro rājā)
rājā
children.translated_text: King:

children.text: rājā --
kāmaṃ priyā na sulabhā manas tu tadbhāvadarśanāśvāsi /
children.translated_text: Though the beloved is not easily won, yet my heart is consoled by seeing signs of her affection;

children.text: akṛtārthe 'pi manasije ratim ubhayaprārthanā kurute //
children.translated_text: even when <s>Kāma</s> has not achieved his goal, longing shared by both makes for delight.

children.text: kāmaṃ priyā na sulabhā manas tu tad-bhāva-darśana-āśvāsi /
akṛta-arthe 'pi manasije ratim ubhaya-prārthanā kurute //
(smitaṃ kṛtvā) evam ātmābhiprāyasaṃbhāviteṣṭajanacittavṛttiḥ prārthitā viḍambyate /
children.translated_text: (Smiling) Thus one whose beloved's feelings are estimated by one's own hopes is made a fool of by desire.

children.text: (smitaṃ kṛtvā) evam ātma-abhiprāya-saṃbhāvita-iṣṭa-jana-citta-vṛttiḥ prārthitā viḍambyate /
snigdhaṃ vīkṣitam anyato 'pi nayane yat prerayantyā tayā
yātaṃ yac ca nitambayor gurutayā mandaṃ vilāsād iva /
children.translated_text: her gait made slow as if by the heaviness of her hips, though really from coquetry,
The tender glance she cast elsewhere while directing her eyes away from me,

children.text: mā gā ity uparuddhayā yad api sā sāsūyam uktā sakhī
sarvaṃ tat kila matparāyaṇam aho kāmī svatāṃ paśyati //
children.translated_text: all that was surely directed at me. Ah, the lover sees everything as meant for himself!
and her friend whom she scolded with jealousy when stopped with "Don't go!"—

children.text: snigdhaṃ vīkṣitam anyato 'pi nayane yat prerayantyā tayā
yātaṃ yac ca nitambayor gurutayā mandaṃ vilāsād iva /
mā gā ity uparuddhayā yad api sā sāsūyam uktā sakhī
sarvaṃ tat kila mat-parāyaṇam aho kāmī svatāṃ paśyati //
vidūṣaka  (tathāsthita eva) bho vayasya na me hastapādaṃ prasarati tad vān mātreṇa jāpayiṣyāmi / jayatu jayatu bhavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Remaining in the same posture) Friend, my hands and feet won't move. So I shall honor you by words alone. Victory, victory to you!

children.text: vidūṣaka -- (tathā-sthita eva) bho vayasya na me hasta-pādaṃ prasarati tad vān mātreṇa jāpayiṣyāmi / jayatu jayatu bhavān /
rājā  kuto 'yaṃ gātropaghātaḥ /
children.translated_text: King: What is this affliction of your limbs?

children.text: rājā -- kuto 'yaṃ gātra-upaghātaḥ /
vidu  kutaḥ kila svayam akṣyākulīkṛtyāśrukāraṇaṃ pṛcchasi /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: What indeed! You yourself poke me in the eyes and then ask the cause of tears!

children.text: vidu -- kutaḥ kila svayam akṣy-ākulī-kṛtya-aśru-kāraṇaṃ pṛcchasi /
rā  na khalv avagacchāmi /
children.translated_text: King: I don't understand.

children.text: rā -- na khalv avagacchāmi /
vidu  bho vayasya yad vetasaḥ kubjalīlāṃ viḍambayati tat kim ātmanaḥ prabhāveṇa nanu nadīvegasya /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: My friend, when a reed-stalk imitates the posture of a hunchback, is that by its own power or by the force of the river's current?

children.text: vidu -- bho vayasya yad vetasaḥ kubja-līlāṃ viḍambayati tat kim ātmanaḥ prabhāveṇa nanu nadī-vegasya /
rā  nadīvegas tatra kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: King: The river's current is the cause.

children.text: rā -- nadī-vegas tatra kāraṇam /
vidu  mama api bhavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: And you are mine.

children.text: vidu -- mama api bhavān /
rā  katham iva /
children.translated_text: King: How so?

children.text: rā -- katham iva /

vidu  evaṃ rājakāryāṇy ujjhitvaitādṛśa ākulapradeśe vanacaravṛttinā tvayā bhavitavyam / yat satyaṃ pratyahaṃ śvāpadasamutsāraṇaiḥ saṃkṣobhitasaṃdhibandhānāṃ mama gātrāṇām anīśo 'smi saṃvṛttaḥ / tat prasīda me / ekāham api tāvad viśramyatām /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Thus—abandoning royal duties, you must live the life of a forest-dweller in such a wretched place! In truth, from the daily chasing away of wild beasts, the joints and ligaments of my body have been so shattered that I have become helpless. So have mercy on me! Let there be at least one day of rest.

children.text: vidu -- evaṃ rāja-kāryāṇy ujjhitva aitādṛśa ākula-pradeśe vana-cara-vṛttinā tvayā bhavitavyam / yat satyaṃ pratyahaṃ śvā-pada-samutsāraṇaiḥ saṃkṣobhita-saṃdhi-bandhānāṃ mama gātrāṇām anīśo 'smi saṃvṛttaḥ / tat prasīda me / eka āham api tāvad viśramyatām /
rājā  (svagatam) ayaṃ caivam āha / mama api kāśyapasutām anusmṛtya mṛgayāviklavaṃ cetaḥ / kutaḥ
children.translated_text: King: (Aside) He says this, and I too, when I recall the daughter of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, find my heart shaken out of the fervor of the hunt. For—

children.text: rājā -- (svagatam) ayaṃ ca evam āha / mama api kāśyapa-sutām anusmṛtya mṛgayā-viklavaṃ cetaḥ / kutaḥ
na namayitum adhijyam asmi śakto dhanur idam āhitasāyakaṃ mṛgeṣu /
children.translated_text: I am unable to bend this bow, with arrow fitted, against the deer

children.text: sahavasatim upetya yaiḥ priyāyāḥ kṛta iva mugdhavilokopadeśaḥ //
children.translated_text: who share the dwelling of my beloved and who seem to have taught her the art of the innocent glance.

children.text: na namayitum adhijyam asmi śakto dhanur idam āhita-sāyakaṃ mṛgeṣu /
saha-vasatim upetya yaiḥ priyāyāḥ kṛta iva mugdha-viloka-upadeśaḥ //
vidu  (rājño mukhaṃ vilokya) atrabhavān kim api hṛdaye kṛtvā mantrayate / araṇye mayā ruditam āsīt /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: (Looking at the king's face) His honor is pondering something in his heart. My crying in the wilderness was in vain.

children.text: vidu -- (rājño mukhaṃ vilokya) atra-bhavān kim api hṛdaye kṛtvā mantrayate / araṇye mayā ruditam āsīt /
rā  (sasmitam) kim anyat / anatikramaṇīyaṃ me suhṛdvākyam iti sthito 'smi /
children.translated_text: King: (With a smile) What else? I was just resolving that a friend's word must not be disobeyed.

children.text: rā -- (sasmitam) kim anyat / anatikramaṇīyaṃ me suhṛd-vākyam iti sthito 'smi /
vidu  ciraṃ jīva / (iti gantum ichati)
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Long may you live! (Starts to leave.)

children.text: vidu -- ciraṃ jīva / (iti gantum ichati)
rā  vayasya tiṣṭha / sāvaśeṣaṃ me vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: King: Wait, friend! My speech is not yet finished.

children.text: rā -- vayasya tiṣṭha / sāvaśeṣaṃ me vacaḥ /
vidu  ājñāpayatu bhavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Command, sir.

children.text: vidu -- ājñāpayatu bhavān /
rā  viśrāntena bhavatā mama apy ekasminn anāyāse karmaṇi sahāyena bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: King: When you are rested, you must assist me in a certain effortless task.

children.text: rā -- viśrāntena bhavatā mama apy ekasminn anāyāse karmaṇi sahāyena bhavitavyam /
vidu  kiṃ modakakhādikāyām / tena hy ayaṃ sugṛhītaḥ kṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: Is it eating sweetmeats? Then this moment is well seized!

children.text: vidu -- kiṃ modaka-khādikāyām / tena hy ayaṃ sugṛhītaḥ kṣaṇaḥ /
rā  yatra vakṣyāmi / kaḥ ko 'tra bhoḥ /
children.translated_text: King: I shall tell you where. Ho there, who is present?

children.text: rā -- yatra vakṣyāmi / kaḥ ko 'tra bhoḥ /
(praviśya)
children.translated_text: (Entering)

children.text: (praviśya)
dauvārika  (praṇamya) ājñāpayatu bharttā /
children.translated_text: Doorkeeper: (Bowing) Command me, master.

children.text: dauvārika -- (praṇamya) ājñāpayatu bharttā /
rā  raivataka senāpatis tāvad āhūyatām /
children.translated_text: King: <s>Raivataka</s>, let the general be summoned.

children.text: rā -- raivataka senā-patis tāvad āhūyatām /
dau  tathā / (iti niṣkramya senāpatinā saha punaḥ praviśya) eṣa ājñāvacanotkaṇṭho bhartetodattadṛṣṭir eva tiṣṭhati / upasarpatv āryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Doorkeeper: As you wish. (Exits, then re-enters with the general.) Here he stands, eyes raised in eager expectation of your command. Let the noble sir approach.

children.text: dau -- tathā / (iti niṣkramya senā-patinā saha punaḥ praviśya) eṣa ājñā-vacana-utkaṇṭho bharta īto-datta-dṛṣṭir eva tiṣṭhati / upasarpatv āryaḥ /
seenā  (rājānam avalokya) dṛṣṭadoṣā api svāmini mṛgayā kevalaṃ guṇa eva saṃvṛttā / tathā hi devaḥ
children.translated_text: General: (Looking at the king) Even though the hunt is seen to have faults, in the master it has become nothing but a virtue. For the lord—

children.text: seenā -- (rājānam avalokya) dṛṣṭa-doṣā api svāmini mṛgayā kevalaṃ guṇa eva saṃvṛttā / tathā hi devaḥ
anavaratadhanur jyāsphālanakrūrapūrva ravikiraṇasahiṣṇu svedaleśair abhinam /
children.translated_text: His body, first hardened by the constant cruel slapping of the bowstring, patient of the sun's rays, glistening slightly with drops of perspiration,

children.text: apacitam api gātraṃ vyāyatatvād alakṣyaṃ giricara iva nāgaḥ prāṇasāraṃ bibharti //
children.translated_text: though lean, unnoticeable due to its muscularity, like a mountain-roaming elephant, bears the essence of life-force!
